outcomes.text: Name the four factors of production: land, labour, capital and enterprise.
Explain what adding value means and how a business can add more value.
Explain opportunity cost and give examples of choices that involve it.
Tell the primary, secondary and tertiary sectors apart and place businesses in them.
Tell private-sector from public-sector organisations.
Describe the qualities of successful entrepreneurs.
State what a business plan is for and list its main parts.
Explain why a business plan matters to a start-up.
Explain why governments want to support new businesses.
Describe ways governments help start-ups, such as grants, advice, cheap loans and training.
Name ways to measure business size, such as employees, sales value, sales volume and capital employed.
Explain the problems of measuring business size.

subtopics.title: Why businesses grow or stay small

outcomes.text: Explain why owners may want their business to grow.
Describe internal growth, such as new products and new markets.
Describe external growth through mergers and takeovers, horizontal and vertical integration.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of growth methods.
Explain problems that come with growth.
Explain why some businesses choose or need to stay small.
Explain why businesses succeed or fail, e.g. management skills, finance, product, demand, economy and competition.
Describe sole traders, partnerships, private limited and public limited companies.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of each legal form.
Recommend and justify a suitable form of organisation for a given situation.

subtopics.title: Franchises, joint ventures and social enterprises

outcomes.text: Describe franchises, joint ventures and social enterprises.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of franchises for franchisor and franchisee.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of joint ventures.
Describe common objectives such as survival, growth, profit and market share.
Explain why having objectives matters to a business.
Name internal stakeholders: owners, managers and employees.
Name external stakeholders: customers, suppliers, lenders, government and the local community.
Describe what different stakeholder groups want from a business.
Explain how stakeholder objectives can conflict.
Describe the recruitment steps: job description, person specification and job advert.
Describe selection methods such as CVs, application forms, references, tests and interviews.
Weigh internal against external recruitment.
Recommend and justify who to employ in a given situation.
State what an employment contract contains.
Explain how contracts benefit employers and employees.
Describe legal controls on unfair dismissal, discrimination, health and safety and minimum wage.
Explain how these legal controls affect employers and employees.
Explain why training matters to a business and its employees.
Describe induction, on-the-job and off-the-job training.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of the three types of training.
Name the main functional areas: operations, marketing, finance and human resources.
Describe tall and flat hierarchies, chains of command and spans of control.
Read a simple organisation chart.
Describe flexible working such as home working and flexible hours.
Weigh part-time against full-time employees.
Describe the management functions: planning, organising, coordinating, commanding and controlling.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of delegation.
Describe autocratic, democratic and laissez-faire leadership.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of each style.
Recommend and justify a leadership style for a given situation.
Explain downsizing.
Give reasons for cutting the workforce, such as automation, falling demand and cost cutting.
Explain redundancy.
Recommend and justify which employees to make redundant in a given case.
Explain what a trade union is.
Describe how employees benefit from joining a union.
Explain why communication is important to a business.
Describe methods such as meetings, email, texts, social media, calls, letters and notice boards.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of different methods.
Tell internal from external communication.
Recommend and justify a method of communication for a given situation.
Give examples of communication barriers and their causes.
Explain the problems barriers cause.
Describe how barriers can be reduced or removed.
Explain why people work.
Describe the benefits of a motivated workforce: productivity, less absence, lower turnover and openness to change.
Outline the motivation theories of Maslow, Taylor and Herzberg.
Describe financial methods: time rate, piece rate, salary, bonus, commission, profit sharing and fringe benefits.
Describe non-financial methods: job enrichment, rotation, training, promotion, praise and employee of the month.
Recommend and justify a motivation method for a given situation.
Explain how marketing identifies and satisfies customer needs.
Explain how marketing keeps customers loyal and builds relationships.
Explain why businesses must anticipate changing customer needs.
Explain why consumer spending patterns change.
Explain why some markets become more competitive.
Describe how businesses can respond to changing spending and more competition.
Calculate market share.
Explain mass markets and niche markets.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of each.
Describe segmenting a market by age, income, location, gender and lifestyle.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of segmentation.
Explain why businesses carry out market research.
Describe primary methods: surveys, interviews, focus groups and observation.
Explain sampling and why it is useful.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of primary research.
Describe secondary sources such as competitor websites, government data, market reports and trade magazines.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of secondary research.
Explain what affects the accuracy of research data.
Analyse simple market research data.
Explain why brand image matters.
Describe the role of packaging.
Weigh the pros and cons of developing new products.
Describe the introduction, growth, maturity and decline stages.
Read a product life cycle diagram.
Describe extension strategies: new markets, new uses, adapting the product or packaging, and more promotion.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of extension strategies.
Recommend and justify an extension strategy for a given situation.
Describe cost-plus, competitive, penetration, skimming and dynamic pricing.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of each pricing method.
Recommend and justify a pricing method for a given situation.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of selling direct, via retailers, wholesalers or agents.
Recommend and justify a distribution channel for a given situation.
Give reasons why businesses promote products.
Describe sales promotion methods such as vouchers, rewards, competitions and discounts.
Describe advertising methods such as social media, targeted emails, leaflets and billboards.
Recommend and justify a sales promotion method for a given situation.
Recommend and justify an advertising method for a given situation.
Give examples of ecommerce, such as online banking, shopping and ticketing.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of ecommerce for businesses.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of ecommerce for customers.

subtopics.title: Marketing strategy and new overseas markets

outcomes.text: Explain the importance of each element of the marketing mix.
Recommend and justify a marketing mix for a given situation.
Describe the advantages of entering new markets abroad, such as more sales and spread risk.
Describe the disadvantages, such as cultural differences, lack of knowledge and legal rules.
Explain why laws protect customers from misleading promotion and faulty goods.
Explain how legal controls affect marketing.
Calculate labour productivity.
Explain why efficiency matters to a business.
Describe ways to raise efficiency, e.g. automation and better skills.
Explain lean production and how just-in-time and Kaizen achieve it.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of lean production.
Explain why businesses hold inventory.
Describe factors that affect how much inventory is held.
Describe job, batch and flow production.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of each method.
Recommend and justify a production method for a given situation.

topics.title: 4.2 Technology and production of goods and services

outcomes.text: Explain how automation, mechanisation, CAM and 3D printing change production.
Explain how technology raises productivity in services, e.g. contactless payments.
Weigh the pros and cons of technological change for businesses and employees.

topics.title: 4.3 Sustainable production of goods and services

outcomes.text: Describe ways to be more sustainable: renewable energy, less waste, reuse, recycling, greener products and packaging.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of becoming more sustainable.

topics.title: 4.4 Costs, scale of production and break-even analysis

outcomes.text: Classify and calculate fixed, variable, average and total costs.
Use cost data to decide which product to make, whether to stop, what price to set and which supplier to choose.
Describe economies of scale: purchasing, marketing, financial, managerial and technical.
Describe diseconomies of scale: poor communication, low loyalty, weak coordination and lack of control.
Explain the idea of break-even.
Complete or amend a simple break-even chart.
Interpret a break-even chart.
Calculate break-even output.

subtopics.title: Margin of safety and break-even decisions

outcomes.text: Define, calculate and interpret the margin of safety.
Use break-even to judge changes in price, fixed costs or variable cost per unit.
Describe the limitations of break-even analysis.
Explain what quality means and why it matters.
Explain quality control.
Explain quality assurance.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of each.
Recommend and justify quality control or assurance for a given situation.
Describe factors that affect where a manufacturer locates.
Describe factors that affect where a service business locates.
Describe factors in choosing which country to operate in.
Recommend and justify a location for a given business.
Give reasons businesses need finance: start-up, expansion, replacing assets, new technology and working capital.
Tell short-term from long-term finance needs.
Explain working capital and why it matters.
Describe internal sources: owners' money, retained profit, asset sales and working capital.
Describe external sources: shares, venture capital, overdrafts, leasing, hire purchase, loans, trade credit, grants and crowdfunding.
Weigh internal against external sources.
Describe factors for choosing a source of finance, such as size, legal form, amount, time, cost and purpose.
Recommend and justify a source of finance for a given situation.
Explain why cash matters to a business.
Explain what a cash flow forecast is and why it is useful.
Name its features: inflow, outflow, net cash flow, opening and closing balance.
Amend or complete a simple cash flow forecast.
Interpret a simple cash flow forecast.
Describe ways to fix a short-term cash problem, such as overdraft or slower supplier payments.
Explain what profit is.
Explain why private-sector firms need profit: reward for risk, finance, measure of success and attracting investors.
Describe its features: revenue, cost of sales, gross profit, expenses and profit.
Make simple calculations from a statement of profit or loss.
Make decisions using simple statements of profit or loss.
Tell non-current from current assets, with examples.
Tell non-current from current liabilities, with examples.
Explain capital employed.
Calculate total assets, total liabilities and working capital.
Make decisions using simple statements of financial position.
Explain profitability.
Calculate and interpret gross profit margin, profit margin and ROCE.
Explain liquidity.
Calculate and interpret the current ratio and acid test ratio.
Describe how internal users such as owners, managers and employees use accounts.
Describe how external users such as suppliers, government and lenders use accounts.
Explain how financial information supports decisions such as lending or investing.
Describe the limitations of accounts and ratio analysis.
Describe the stages: growth, boom, recession and slump.
Explain how each stage affects a business.
Explain how employment, inflation and growth changes affect a business.
Explain how tax changes affect business profit.
Explain how tax changes affect people's income.
Explain how changes in government spending affect business.
Explain how interest rate changes affect business.
Describe how businesses respond to tax and interest rate changes.
Describe reasons for globalisation: transport, technology, free trade deals and newly industrialised countries.
Describe opportunities and threats of globalisation for businesses.
Explain import tariffs and quotas.
Explain how tariffs and quotas affect businesses.
Describe the advantages of becoming a multinational.
Describe advantages of hosting an MNC, such as jobs, exports, choice and investment.
Describe disadvantages of hosting an MNC, such as competition, environmental damage and profits sent abroad.
Explain external costs and external benefits of business decisions.
Explain appreciation and depreciation of an exchange rate.
Explain how exchange rate changes affect importers and exporters.
Explain how business activity can harm the environment.
Explain why businesses respond to environmental issues.
Describe how businesses respond to environmental issues.
Explain how environmental laws affect what, how and where businesses produce and sell, and their costs.
Give examples of ethical issues, such as child labour, fair wages and fair supplier prices.
Describe how businesses respond to ethical issues.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of acting ethically.
Explain what a pressure group is.
Explain how pressure groups can influence business decisions.
